articles.standfirst: Segundo informações da Artesp, um VW Polo cruzou a pista e atingiu uma Fiat Toro na noite de sábado (19). Vias ficaram interditadas e foram liberadas na madrugada deste domingo (20).
articles.summary: Segundo informações da Artesp, um VW Polo cruzou a pista e atingiu uma Fiat Toro na noite de sábado (19). Vias ficaram interditadas e foram liberadas na madrugada de domingo (20).
articles.body:
Imagem de arquivo da Rodovia do Açúcar (SP-308), na região de Piracicaba. — Foto: Divulgação/Rodovias do Tietê

Duas pessoas morreram após uma batida entre um carro e uma picape na noite de sábado (19), na Rodovia do Açúcar (SP-308), em Elias Fausto (SP). O acidente aconteceu na altura do km 117.

Segundo informações da Agência de Transporte do Estado de São Paulo (Artesp), um VW Polo cruzou a pista e atingiu uma Fiat Toro.

As duas vítimas que estavam no Polo morreram no local do acidente. As identidades não foram divulgadas até a publicação desta reportagem.

Outras três pessoas que ocupavam o veículo ficaram levemente feridas, e dois ocupantes da Fiat Toro saíram ilesos.

Por conta do acidente, as duas pistas da rodovia ficaram totalmente interditadas durante o trabalho das equipes de resgate e atendimento da ocorrência. A liberação ocorreu na madrugada deste domingo (20).

articles.title: Senior journalist Payal Mehta passes away at age of 46; PM Modi, Amit Shah offer condolences
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Senior journalist Payal Mehta, who worked with CNN-News18, died in Mumbai in the early hours of Sunday. She was 46.Mehta was visiting Mumba.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Senior journalist Payal Mehta, who worked with CNN-News18, died in Mumbai in the early hours of Sunday. She was 46.Mehta was visiting Mumbai when she developed uneasiness around 2 am. She was taken to a hospital, but died before treatment could begin.Senior journalist Sheela Bhatt shared the details in a post on X."On a visit to Mumbai, she developed uneasiness. Around 2 am she was taken to the hospital. Before any treatment could be administered, her pulse went silent".Mehta was known for her work covering Parliament, the government and the BJP. Colleagues and senior political leaders remembered her as a dedicated journalist who closely followed national affairs.Prime Minister Narendra Modi, home minister Amit Shah, defence minister Rajnath Singh, Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma and several Union ministers expressed condolences following her death."Payal Mehta Ji was a hardworking journalist who remained firmly connected to the ground, bringing a deep understanding of national issues to her reporting," Modi said in a post on X.He added that Mehta would also be remembered for her kindness and the warmth she showed towards others."Her sudden and untimely passing is extremely saddening. My condolences to her family, friends and colleagues. May they find strength in this difficult hour. Om Shanti," he said.Shah described Mehta as a thorough professional who was committed to providing detailed information on a range of issues."I extend my deepest condolences to her grieving family and friends and pray to God to give them the strength to bear this profound pain. Om Shanti," he said in a post on X.Singh said he was deeply shocked by her death and recalled her commitment to the Parliament beat."She has left us far too soon. Payal was an extremely hardworking and dedicated journalist who covered the Parliament beat with great commitment and professionalism," he said.He recalled that Mehta would often remain in Parliament from early morning until late at night during sessions, closely following proceedings."My heartfelt condolences to her family and friends in this difficult hour. May they find the strength to bear this irreparable loss. Om Shanti," he said.Railways and Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw also expressed grief over the death of his "journalist and dear friend Payal Mehta"."Her dedication to reporting was exemplary. Om Shanti," he said.Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said he was deeply shocked by the news."Had just attended her father's prayer service a few days ago. Payal used to be as regular as me in Parliament during sessions. She was a true professional journalist. Heartfelt prayers for her departed soul. Om Shanti," Rijiju said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Delhi SIR: Jaishankar, Dhankhar, Advani among those issued notices
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Several well-known VIP faces in politics and in govt have got notices for various SIR “discrepancies” in Delhi.Among them are former Indian.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Several well-known VIP faces in politics and in govt have got notices for various SIR “discrepancies” in Delhi.Among them are former Indian Vice-President Jagdeep Dhankhar, BJP veteran LK Advani, former Delhi deputy chief minister Manish Sisodia, foreign minister S Jaishankar, election commissioner Sukhbir Singh Sandhu, foreign secretary Vikram Misri, former NITI Aayog vice-chairman Arvind Panagariya, SEBI chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey, BJP MLA Kailash Gahlot, former army chief Upendra Dwevedi, CBI director Praveen Sood and former Delhi LG Najeeb Jung.Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta has been sent a notice for an age discrepancy. Former CM Arvind Kejriwal also has got a notice, but for being an unmapped voter.Bibek Debroy, a former chairman of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister, who passed away in 2024, has also been served an SIR notice. His name was also included in the draft rolls published on Aug 31. “The late Bibek Debroy’s name appeared on the flagged list which included prominent voters. As per the ECI’s instructions, names on the flagged list, including those of VVIPs and VIPs, are retained in the draft rolls so that the required documents can be collected during the claims and objections process. We are aware of his death and his name will be excluded from the final list,” an official said.Those issued the notices are among the 97.5 lakh voters included in the draft SIR roll released on Aug 31. Of them, about 33 lakh have been found to have some kind of discrepancy. So far, the poll panel has issued notices to 31.6 lakh people and uploaded the lists of such voters on its website.More than half of those served notices have “logical discrepancies”, such as mismatches in names and inconsistencies in age or family details. The rest were listed for “no mapping” with previous SIR of 2002. The “logical discrepancies” have been identified by the system.Advani, daughter Pratibha Advani and daughter-in-law Geetika have been flagged under the “no mapping” category, which means their names could not be linked to the 2002 SIR.Sandhu has been served the notice for a “name mismatch”, while Misri is in the “unmapped” category. The New Delhi district election office said that in Sandhu’s case “the details... furnished by the elector have been verified. The entry pertaining to SS Sandhu has already been validated”.Sisodia, his wife Seema and son Meer have got notices over “name mismatch” and “discrepancy in his parents’ names”. Gahlot has been marked under “no mapping” category.Delhi CEO’s office Sunday clarified that no name will be deleted without giving voters an opportunity to be heard.“These electors may submit a reply to the ERO/BLO. EROs will take the final decision on case-by-case basis.... Disposal of notices will be completed by 29.10.2026 and the names of electors will be included in the final electoral roll to be published on 04.11.2026,” the CEO office said.Lawyer Kapil Sibal, who is on the list, said the SIR was a “special intensive deletion” to remove valid voters and add invalid voters.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: IIT-Bombay suicide case: Institute director Shireesh Kedare meets protesting students, ‘signs’ list of 18 demands
articles.summary: IIT Bombay director met protesting students over Sahil Wakode’s suicide, signed 18 demands; Board of Governors to meet as students seek professor’s suspension.
articles.body: MUMBAI: In a late-night three-hour meeting on Sunday, IIT-Bombay director Shireesh Kedare spoke to the students who gathered in large numbers at the institute’s main gate to protest against the death by suicide of BTech student Sahil Wakode (20).In the meeting, which was recorded live by the students, the institute’s administration discussed 18 demands put forth by the protesters and signed it. An institute official said that the discussions will continue and “due process will be followed”.The institute’s Board of Governors is scheduled to meet on Monday to discuss the issue. An open house with students is also expected to be held on the same day.Protests erupted on the Powai campus on Friday night after Wakode, a second-year student of energy science and engineering, ended his life hours after he was caught using a mobile phone during the institute’s mid-semester examination. He allegedly uploaded the exam paper on an AI platform for answers. This was the third case of suicide on the campus this year.While the institute, in a statement, mentioned that no action was initiated against Wakode, many claimed that he was threatened with suspension.Among students’ demands, suspension of Prof Suryanarayana Doolla, Sahil’s teacher and also the invigilator of the exam, was the foremost.Sahil’s family had filed an FIR against Doolla and ‘other institute officials’, accusing them of abetment and harassment over the last three months. The students also asked for an open apology for ‘defaming’ Sahil and an open house with all the stakeholders before Sept 22. The list of demands also includes an independent investigation committee with student representatives and external members recommended by them, suspension of officials who are found guilty after the probe, and a fair compensation for the families. Students have also sought a code of conduct and sensitisation for professors.Amid the ongoing protest, IIT-B’s faculty forum has come out in support of Doolla. In a statement issued on Sunday, the forum, while mourning the loss of life of the student and extending condolences to the family, strongly expressed their solidarity with the professor.The forum said, “...the professor was discharging his duties in line with the institute’s Senate approved academic policies currently in force”. It added, “Prof Doolla was invigilating in the examination on Friday, when he observed that a student was indulging in an academic malpractice... As part of the institute approved procedure, he reported the incident to institute authorities for further action in the matter.”The faculty forum added that they are distressed with the tarnishing of the reputation of their colleague who was merely discharging his duties.Meanwhile, the institute is planning to replace the ceiling fans with wall-mounted ones in its student hostels. Sources said the plan had been under consideration for the past two months and was finalised recently. The first batch of wall-mounted fans seemed to have arrived on campus, students claimed.Replacing the fans was among the measures the institute had assured students it would undertake in July, following the death by suicide of another student from the same hostel.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Bengal SIR tribunals may take 12 years to decide on appeals
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The innumerable voters in West Bengal who were removed from the electoral rolls after special intensive revision (SIR) may not be able to v.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The innumerable voters in West Bengal who were removed from the electoral rolls after special intensive revision (SIR) may not be able to vote for more than a decade as appellate tribunals set up by Supreme Court could take more than 12 years to decide on their appeals for inclusion, going by the present pace of adjudication.An affidavit filed by Election Commission before Supreme Court says 1,26,194 applications have been decided by tribunals in the last five months since they started functioning in mid-April. So, on average, 25,238 cases are being decided by the tribunals in a month when even Saturdays and Sundays are included as working days. The total number of pending cases as of Sept 16, when the affidavit was filed, was 37,05,235. At current speed, if the tribunals work seven days a week, it would take 146 months to decide all cases.Admitting that the present infrastructure and number of tribunals are insufficient to handle the Herculean task of adjudicating 37 lakh cases, the poll panel pleaded with the court to increase the number of tribunals in the state from 24 to 42, almost double the present strength, and allow judicial officers to work from home."With a view to further streamlining and expediting the disposal of the pending appeals, it is proposed that the number of appellate tribunals in the state of West Bengal may be considered for increase to correspond with the number of parliamentary constituencies in the state, so as to facilitate expeditious disposal of the pending appeals," said the affidavit, filed in response to a petition from TMC MP Derek O' Brien. Allowing judicial workers to conduct hearings and undertake other proceedings from home "would assist in expediting the disposal of pending appeals by minimising the time lost in conveyance", it said.In another affidavit filed in response to a petition on the functioning of the tribunals, the commission said they were constituted pursuant to the directives of the apex court and the standard operating procedure (SOP) governing their functioning has been formulated by the committee constituted for this purpose, comprising, inter alia, former judges of the high court at Calcutta."It is humbly submitted that the reliefs sought by the petitioner pertain primarily to the functioning, procedure and accessibility of the appellate mechanism and, therefore, fall within the domain of the SOP governing the functioning of the appellate tribunals and the authorities entrusted with the administration thereof. The feasibility, modalities and implementation... are matters best left to the consideration of the concerned appellate tribunal..." the affidavit said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Sri Lanka's Chemmani mass grave reopens wounds from the civil war - and families want answers
articles.summary: Workers in northern Sri Lanka accidentally uncovered the country's largest mass grave – and reopened wounds from its civil war.
articles.body:
When a mass grave was unearthed in northern Sri Lanka last February, it was not by design.

Workers were digging to extend a cremation ground in the Chemmani area of the Jaffna region when they suddenly discovered human remains, prompting an investigation.

By August, archaeologists had completed the third phase of the excavation at the site, during which they found the skeletal remains of 572 people, including children and infants.

Among the dead were artefacts from their lives – bangles, a school bag, a milk bottle.

It is believed to be the largest mass grave site ever uncovered in Sri Lanka.

There had been whispers of its existence before - a soldier on trial for the rape and murder of a young woman during the country's devastating civil war, had spoken about a mass grave which contained hundreds of bodies. Rights groups said they were disappeared civilians

And while the discovery is devastating, it has offered hope to people like Jeyaruby Jeyabalan, whose father was among thousands of people who disappeared during the decades-long war. Jeyabalan and families like his hope that answers about what happened to their loved ones lie among the bodies.

Many Tamils believe the grave holds the victims of extrajudicial killings carried out during the civil war. They are calling for an investigation – and for justice.

But the excavation process at Chemmani has moved slowly, testing the patience of families searching for answers about their disappeared loved ones.

The discovery of hundreds of remains near a previously identified mass grave has fuelled anger among the Tamils, who have long-demanded a thorough inquiry into disappearances.

Many fear the mass grave will eventually fade from public attention because of a lack of political will to pursue the truth – and so the grave has become a rallying point for renewed protests in Sri Lanka's north.

Sri Lanka, particularly the Tamil-dominated north and east, suffered decades of conflict. The war, which lasted from 1983 to 2009, divided the island-nation along ethnic lines. Tamil Tiger rebels fought for an independent state in the north-east of the country due to what they called systematic discrimination by the Sinhalese-dominated government.

The conflict lasted 26 years and the fighting killed an estimated 100,000 people. It also left about 23,000 – mostly Tamils – missing.

Both the security forces and Tamil Tigers are accused of atrocities and crimes .

In 1995, after a bloody conflict, the Sri Lankan army wrested control of the Jaffna Peninsula from the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE). It was seen as a key turning point in the war, which ended with the defeat of the Tigers in 2009.

As they extended control in the late 1990s, the entire Chemmani region became part of a high-security zone and was dotted with army camps, check points and security posts. There was an army camp in Chemmani close to the cemetery as well.

Some at that time described the Jaffna region as an "open prison" - and the security forces were accused of causing the disappearance of thousands of civilians, something Sri Lankan governments have always denied.

"I was 12 years old when my father was picked up by the Sri Lankan army at a checkpoint close to Chemmani area in September 1996. We still don't know what happened to him," Jeyaruby Jayapalan, who now lives in Jaffna, tells the BBC.

She recalls how, after learning of his disappearance, the family panicked and visited military camps and police stations across Jaffna in a desperate search for information without any luck. He never came back.

Her father, Kandaiah Jayapalan, was a government employee who also ran a roadside café not far from Chemmani.

"I went to Chemmani mass grave with many others hoping that I will find some answers. But we didn't find any material evidence. We want a detailed forensic analysis of the human remains," says Jeyaruby.

Two weeks before Kandaiah Jayapalan vanished, an 18-year-old Tamil school girl, Krishanthi Kumaraswamy, disappeared in the same area.

In 1998, a court in Colombo sentenced five soldiers to death for the rape and murder of Kumaraswamy and for killing three of her family members. The case drew global attention at that time. Their bodies were later found buried in Chemmani area .

It is among the most infamous cases from the conflict – and the grave currently under investigation is within 100 metres of the remains of Kumaraswamy and others were found.

In a startling court testimony, one of the convicted soldiers, Somaratne Rajapakse, alleged that between 300 and 400 people who had been killed in the mid-1990s were buried in Chemmani.

His claim led to the first excavation at Chemmani a year later, during which investigators unearthed more than 10 human skeletons. Human rights activists believed those remains were linked to people who had disappeared during the civil war, but there was little judicial follow-up.

Activists say that because the war with the Tamil rebels was ongoing, the then government didn't pursue the investigation and did not explain why.

The discovery of another mass grave in the same area has revived calls for accountability.

"Preliminary inspections suggest this was not a normal burial site and not consistent with ordinary Hindu burial practices," says Gehan Gunatilleke, a commissioner with Human Rights Commission of Sri Lanka, which conducted inspections at Chemmani last year.

Activists and experts say that while a few dozen bodies appeared to have been formally buried, the vast majority told a different story.

Most of the human remains were found without clothing, packed tightly together and, in some cases, stacked on top of others. The graves were shallow, with bodies buried just one to two metres below the surface.

"There is a reasonable likelihood that the burials were unlawful and pursuant to extrajudicial killings," the Human Rights Commission of Sri Lanka said in a report last year.

Past investigations haven't led to prosecutions

The families of those disappeared during the conflict have responded to the discovery by holding protest meetings and remembrance ceremonies.

Among them is Suseela, a 65-year-old woman who is looking for her son, Gnanaseelan Ravi, who was picked up by the Sri Lankan military in 2007, when he was 24.

"He was my only son, and I keep crying every day remembering him. My life is empty without him," she tells the BBC.

She went to Chemmani grave but couldn't find any evidence, likes clothes or personal jewellery, that suggested her son was buried there. DNA tests on the human remains are yet to be carried out.

All the remains recovered so far from Chemmani have been kept in the Forensic Department of the University of Jaffna campus under court custody.

"We are preparing an interim report, and it will be submitted to the court by the end of September," Prof Raj Somadeva, the chief archaeologist of the mass grave told the BBC.

Some of the samples are expected to be sent abroad for detailed examination to help determine the age of the remains. Separate medical analyses will be needed to establish the possible causes of death.

More than 20 mass graves have been found across Sri Lanka in recent decades, but none have been conclusively linked to enforced disappearances or alleged extra-judicial killings in the north and south of the country – and none have led to prosecutions.

Given the failure of the authorities to investigate previous mass graves, there is scepticism among many Tamil people over what the new investigation might achieve.

They point out to the outcome of the investigation on another mass grave was unearthed in the north-western town of Mannar in 2018 in which more than 350 skeletal remains were found. Investigations proved inconclusive, leaving many families disappointed.

They want Sri Lanka to be referred to the International Criminal Court.

The government of President Anura Kumara Dissanayake insists that it is fully cooperating with the investigation.

After coming to power in September 2024, Dissanayake promised to work towards justice and ethnic reconciliation. But his government vehemently opposes any international mechanism to investigate alleged war crimes committed during the ethnic conflict, disappointing Tamils.

"We will continue with the excavation work at Chemmani," Harshana Nanayakkara, Sri Lanka's justice minister told the BBC.

"We need to analyse the skeletons and find out how these people died. Then we have to carry out DNA tests," he said.

The government, he insists, has also asked the families to give their DNA so that it can be analysed later with the remains.

During his inspection at Chemmani in June, the minister promised investigations to find justice and truth to bring an end to the matter. He also promised that necessary funding will be allocated for the excavation.

The Sri Lankan army spokesman, Brigadier Waruna Gamage rejects allegations that security forces buried civilians after massacring them.

"All the allegations should be proved in court," he told the BBC.

The delays in investigating past crimes have attracted stringent criticism from rights groups.

After years of international pressure, in 2018 the government set up an independent body, the Office of the Missing Persons (OMP), to investigate the disappearances. But those affected say it hasn't made much progress in finding their missing relatives.

"Many cases of forced disappearance, torture and killing remain stalled, while families of victims and human rights defenders face threats and intimidation," Human Rights Watch said in a report earlier this month.

The United Nations has urged Sri Lanka to seek international help in identifying the victims, to find out how they died, and who is responsible.

"This is a situation where victims are deeply frustrated, have lived with pain for decades, have come to distrust past investigations," Rory Mungoven, the Asia-Pacific chief at the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights tells the BBC.

"I think involving international assistance would help to bolster confidence in these investigations," he points out.

Successive Sri Lankan governments have strongly resisted calls for international investigations into alleged wartime atrocities.

During earlier reporting trips to Sri Lanka, I met parents and family members of the disappeared who campaigned for decades to the search for truth. Some have since passed away without ever discovering the fates of their loved ones .

Human rights groups say that President Dissanayake's government now has an opportunity to break from a long-standing pattern of delay and denial and deliver accountability for grave abuses committed during the conflict.

Suseela is determined to know the truth.

"I don't know how long I will live with such uncertainty, but I want closure," she says.

Additional Reporting by: Ranjan Arun Prasadh, BBC Tamil Service in Kandy and Kumanan Kanapathippillai in Jaffna.

articles.title: Ruling party dominates early results in Russia’s wartime parliamentary vote
articles.summary: The Kremlin wants the elections to showcase popular support for the war in Ukraine and legitimise its action.
articles.body:
The ruling United Russia party is on course to win the country’s first wartime parliamentary elections, according to early returns from the tightly controlled vote, which was marked by cyberattacks and a barrage of Ukrainian drone attacks.

The Kremlin wants the elections, the first parliamentary vote since the start of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, to showcase popular support for the war and legitimise its action.

Russian government officials accused Ukraine of trying to disrupt voting after Kyiv launched hundreds of drones at Moscow and other regions in what the TASS state news agency said was the biggest attack of its kind since the war began.

The drone strikes on Sunday killed at least three people in the Moscow region and two more in the Russian-held part of Ukraine’s Kherson region, including an election official, according to the region’s governor and the election commission.

Russian authorities also reported attacks on the country’s electronic voting systems and communication lines during the polls, but said the electoral process was mostly smooth.

With some 58 percent of the precincts counted, United Russia had nearly 58 percent of the vote for the 225 deputies apportioned by party lists, according to Russia’s Central Election Commission. Another 225 lawmakers will be chosen in single-seat races, and United Russia was also poised to win most of those.

Authorities said turnout at the close of polls stood at 56.66 percent.

The vote, which began on Friday for 111 million eligible voters, included residents of four Ukrainian regions that Moscow illegally annexed after the war began, but still doesn’t fully control, as well as those in Crimea, the Black Sea peninsula that was illegally annexed by Russia in 2014.

Authorities in Kyiv denounced the voting in the Russian-held areas as illegal and urged foreign governments not to recognise the result. The European Union on Friday called the action a “blatant violation of international law”.

Voters cast two separate ballots, filling half of the lower house’s 450 seats by selecting political parties listed on the ballot. The rest are contested in single-seat constituencies, with voters choosing individual candidates.

The main Kremlin party, United Russia, is widely expected to retain its overwhelming control of the State Duma. Several smaller parties of the “systemic opposition” that vote in sync with Putin’s views on all key issues are also expected to maintain their presence.

A massive state media campaign and tight control over the elections in the absence of genuine opposition all but assure the Kremlin will keep tight control of Russian politics amid mounting economic costs and increasing Ukrainian drone attacks deep inside the country.

The liberal Yabloko party, the only registered political entity that dared to publicly criticise the war, was removed from the ballot last month by Russia’s Supreme Court. It only has a few dozen candidates in the single-constituency races.

Additionally, some anti-war politicians were imprisoned or forced to flee abroad ahead of the campaign.

Russia didn’t invite election observers from the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe. The Russian Foreign Ministry has accused the body of “double standards” for its criticism of Russia.

articles.title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns
articles.summary: The National Association of Head Teachers says inspections in England may pose a "risk to life" for school leaders.
articles.body:
England's biggest school leaders' union has called for a halt to graded Ofsted inspections, saying they could pose a "risk to life" for school staff.

The National Association of Head Teachers (NAHT) said the change to inspections, rolled out nationally just under a year ago, had been severely harmful to school leaders' welfare.

It said schools should instead be rated using short narrative reports that set out their strengths and areas they could improve.

Ofsted said it had worked closely with unions and parents to develop the new report card inspection system, and would continue to grade schools.

Ofsted, England's schools' inspectorate, introduced the report card system to replace its previous one or two-word judgements last November, following the death of head teacher Ruth Perry , who took her own life after Ofsted downgraded her school from "outstanding" to "inadequate".

An inquest ruled that an Ofsted inspection had contributed to her death in January 2023.

That led to a change in how Ofsted assessed schools, bringing in report cards designed to grade schools on several areas, rather than focusing on one overall grade for the whole school.

But the new system faced criticism from when it was first proposed , with Perry's sister, Prof Julia Waters, saying it appeared to be "a rehash of the discredited and dangerous system it is meant to replace".

The NAHT issued a claim with the High Court for a judicial review over the changes, arguing there had not been adequate consultation on the new report cards before they were introduced, but that was rejected.

Nearly a year after it was fully rolled out, the NAHT says evidence from its members suggests the new system is having a detrimental impact on school leaders' mental health.

Testimonies seen by the BBC suggest head teachers are being left "overwhelmed" and "anxious", with the pressure caused by the inspections described as "intolerable".

Although the system had been changed with the intention of lowering the burden on school leaders, the testimonies say the inspection and assessment process had become "higher stakes than ever before".

Amanda Hulme, head teacher at Claypool Primary School in Bolton, said a recent inspection at her school had been "easily the most stressful experience" of her career.

"It was definitely damaging to my health and really quite distressing," she said.

"I couldn't sleep and it led to my blood pressure and pulse rate increasing.

"The effect on my team has also been significant, with some colleagues no longer wanting to pursue headship, and another teacher considering leaving the profession entirely."

The NAHT says it has shared examples with Education Secretary Lucy Powell of some of the "damaging experiences" it says its members have faced.

Speaking to LBC earlier this month, Powell said she took head teacher wellbeing "incredibly seriously" and that the system of accountability needed to be "supportive and understanding.

"I'll continue the work that I do with head teachers, head teacher representatives and others to make sure that we get this Ofsted framework, but also the culture and the whole regime, right," she added.

The NAHT said the results of a recent survey of its members suggested that the majority who responded felt that inspections had worsened in the past 12 months.

The union is now calling for inspections to pause to allow for a "fundamental review of how inspection works", drawing on examples from other nations.

In Wales, the inspectorate Estyn has removed judgements such as "excellent" and "good" from its reports, instead summarising findings by highlighting a school's strengths and areas for improvement.

Northern Ireland's Education and Training Inspectorate (ETI) also uses narrative reports without grades.

Scotland's His Majesty's Inspectorate of Education (HIME) does use grades, but there has been a recent consultation on their use.

NAHT general secretary Paul Whiteman said: "The clear theme emerging across all the feedback we have received is that this Ofsted framework is even more stressful than the one that preceded it.

"It poses a real and present danger to the well-being and mental health of school leaders and teachers, possibly even a risk to life."

He said he welcomed the new education secretary's focus on teacher wellbeing, adding: "Really fundamental changes to inspection are needed, and we stand ready to work with the new government to achieve that."

Responding, Ofsted said it has worked closely with teaching unions over the past three years, to deliver significant reforms and reduce unnecessary pressure on teachers.

"Ofsted exists to raise standards for children and to provide clear reporting to parents," a spokesperson said.

"We will continue to engage closely with trades unions – but we will also continue to grade schools."

articles.title: Will you get £13,000 a year when you stop working? Here's how to check
articles.summary: How to find out how much state pension you're likely to receive - and what you can do about it now.
articles.body:
It may well be decades away, but do you know how much money you will get when you stop working?

The current state pension is soon likely to top £13,000 a year.

Yet one in eight people surveyed by the UK tax authority have never checked how much money they are forecast to receive.

Here's how to find out, and what you can do now to boost it.

If you're working, it is highly likely you're contributing to the state pension - paid by the government when you hit pension age in your late 60s.

the flat-rate state pension - for those who reached state pension age after April 2016 - is £241.30 a week (£12,547.60 a year)

the old basic state pension - for those who reached state pension age before April 2016 - is £184.90 a week (£9,614.80 a year)

Many people on the old basic state pension may receive a top-up called the additional state pension.

Most pensioners have other income, primarily from pension savings built up over their career.

The state pension goes up each year in line with the highest of either inflation, wage increases, or 2.5%. So next April, the flat-rate state pension is expected to go above £13,000 .

Workers pay National Insurance (NI) contributions. In general, you need 35 years of qualifying contributions to get a full state pension.

You may have gaps in your NI record if, for example, you have lived abroad. If you've taken time away from work to care for children or family members, then you get NI credits if you receive child benefit or carer's allowance.

It's possible to boost your contribution history with voluntary payments. Since April 2025, you have only been able to make payments for the previous six years.

That's one reason why it is important to check your state pension forecast well before you retire, experts say.

You can see what you are forecast to receive:

To get a state pension, you will need to prove your identity using official photo ID.

Importantly, never click on a link sent in an unsolicited email or text message, even if it looks official, as it could be a scam.

For more general information about tax and pensions, HMRC has launched a Tax Confident website .

And the government-funded, independent Money Helper website has a free retirement guidance tool to walk you through the options.

The most common reason for not checking a state pension forecast was feeling that retirement was still too far away to think about, a recent survey of 5,000 consumers by HMRC found.

Losing track of pension pots from previous jobs, and concerns about how career breaks might affect their entitlement, were also frequent responses.

People aged 45-54 were the most likely to have never checked.

"Whether retirement is decades away or just around the corner, I'd encourage everyone to check their forecast and see if there's anything they can do now to boost their entitlement later," says Myrtle Lloyd, HMRC's chief customer officer.

articles.title: Sock sensors and smart mattresses - is this the future of dementia care?
articles.summary: Jyoti and Bharat Patel are testing dementia technology including sensors in socks, their bed and around the house.
articles.body:
There are sensors in every room of Jyoti and Bharat Patel's home. Their movements and habits are monitored constantly.

But this doesn't worry them, in fact it gives them peace of mind.

Jyoti was diagnosed with dementia five years ago, and they are now part of an NHS trial using high-tech devices to help patients live at home safely.

The couple, who are in their 70s, are one of more than 250 families participating in the project by the UK Dementia Research Institute (UK DRI).

The hope is that the technology could be extended more widely across the health service, to reduce preventable trips to hospital and give families peace of mind.

Bharat and Jyoti met at a magic show in 1977 and became a double act, with their career leading them to meet King Charles and Princess Anne as well as a host of celebrities.

In 2019, Bharat started noticing that Jyoti was making uncharacteristic mistakes on stage.

"Normally she used to set my stage up and everything was perfect, but I saw something I was looking for and it wasn't there, so I thought something is wrong," he said.

They went to a private health specialist who diagnosed Jyoti with Alzheimer's in 2021.

Jyoti says when she went out, if she did not look around her, she would find that she was lost.

"I didn't know it [was] dementia but I knew it was something which [was] unusual," Bharat says.

In 2023, they were approached by the team at UK Dementia Research Institute and Imperial College London to take part in the trial, which is funded by the medical research charity LifeArc.

Their house in west London is now fitted with different sensors, which are connected via the internet, that send data back to a dedicated team of doctors, nurses and other clinical specialists.

The team then uses the information to better understand how the person is managing their daily routine, identify early signs of changing health and care needs with the hope that they can maintain independence for longer.

Door sensors detect if someone leaves in the middle of the night, movement is monitored to check for signs of a fall, while kitchen appliances are fitted with sensors to check whether Jyoti has eaten and is sticking to her daily routine.

The couple sleep on a "smart mattress" to track sleep disturbances and Jyoti's heart and breathing rates, which can spot early signs of an infection.

Alongside this trial, Jyoti is also testing out smart socks and a special watch that also contain sensors to monitor her body temperature and keep track of any long-term changes in her gait - indicating frailty.

How much will it cost and is it worth it?

Costs are expected to be about £2,000 a year, mainly to cover the monitoring and paying healthcare staff to analyse the data.

If rolled out more widely that could be a significant amount of money with almost a million people living with dementia in the UK.

But Sarah Daniels, health and social care lead at the UK Dementia Research Institute, says the cost is no more than a couple of weeks in a care home.

The main aim, she says, is to give earlier signals to health and social care professionals.

"Earlier signals means earlier intervention, which means we can head potential complications of an infection, potential challenges around care, we can head that off before it becomes a crisis," says Daniels.

None of the devices record sound or video, protecting the individual's privacy, however, some people may feel nervous about the amount of data they are allowing other people to access.

Daniels argues that by enhancing the level of information you provide to your GP, it enables them to make better decisions about your care.

The number of people with dementia in the UK is expected to climb by another 40% by 2040, so the hope is to extend it more widely across the health service.

Dr Jeremy Isaacs, national clinical director for dementia and older people's mental health at NHS England, said the health service would be closely monitoring the trial and said the research built on NHS programmes which were already supporting people to remain more independent in their own homes.

While some people might feel uneasy about having all these sensors in their home, Bharat says they give him greater "peace of mind".

"Even if it can cut down my worries by 5 or 10%, then it helps me and it will help other people too," he says.

articles.title: Brigitte Bardot's ballet flats and diamond rings to be sold at auction
articles.summary: Many of the film star's personal items, on sale in Paris, are priced at under €100.
articles.body:
Personal possessions of late actress Brigitte Bardot – from Repetto ballet flats and diamond rings to her copy of the Kama Sutra – are being sold at auction on Monday with proceeds going to her animal charity.

Fans of the iconic figure, who died last December at the age of 91, have been coming en masse to contemplate the nearly 300 lots on display at the Drouot sale rooms in central Paris.

The items are from Bardot's two homes in Saint-Tropez as well as her Paris flat, parts of which are recreated in the display.

"Each item on sale bears the trace of an encounter, an involvement, a moment of happiness, a stage of her life. They tell the story of the woman as well as the legend," said her secretary for many years, Frank Guillou.

Bardot is seen today as one of the most important female personalities of the late 20th century. As a model and actress from the 1950s, she became an emblem of modern femininity and the sexual revolution before later taking up the cause of animal rights.

But later in life she was also criticised for making homophobic slurs and was fined multiple times for inciting racial hatred.

Monday's auction is a chance to acquire everyday objects that were once her intimate belongings. Along with furniture, clothing and religious statuary, kitchen utensils, Le Creuset pans and cigarette lighters are on offer.

Other highlights include the manual typewriter she used to write her correspondence and autobiography, jewellery, and classical guitars.

Her Peugeot bicycle is on sale, as are two pairs of leather Repetto ballet flats. A trained ballerina, Bardot helped popularise the Repetto brand after asking the company to make her a version for everyday use.

The sale also features a large selection of portraits of the star, some erotic.

"Brigitte used to say that she didn't want to have to look at her mug all day, so they weren't up on the walls - but she did keep them, either because she knew the artists or because the pictures meant something to her. They were all gifts," said Guillou.

Most lots have starting prices of under €100 (£86), but bidding is expected to push these up considerably, according to Cecile Dupuis of the auction-house Millon, which is running the sale.

"[The sale] is for all those people who still live with her memory and who keep her cause alive. They are animal lovers and Brigitte Bardot lovers at the same time. The room will be full of all these fans," she said.

Many items on sale reveal her adoration of animals, including a large selection of cuddly toys and collars that belonged to her dogs.

"Brigitte could not live without animals around her. When one of them died, she was totally wiped out with grief. They were all buried according to a strict protocol in the gardens, and their photographs had pride of place in her homes," said Guillou.

When she died in December, Bardot's estate was divided between her Foundation and her only son Nicolas-Jacques Charrier - who also benefits from the sale.

articles.title: Lindsay Clancy holdout juror makes new promise as lawyer warns of public attacks
articles.summary: Lindsay Clancy's mistrial juror Michael P. Desronvil plans a personal statement while her defense team pursues a double jeopardy dismissal motion.
articles.body: The lone juror who blocked a verdict in Lindsay Clancy’s triple-murder trial has promised to tell his story in his own words as his attorney warns that jurors must be allowed to follow the evidence without fear of retaliation. Attorney Edward Paltzik said Michael P. Desronvil, whose refusal to join the other 11 jurors led to a mistrial, will issue a personal statement in the "near future." "Michael will be making a personal statement in the near future, in his own words," Paltzik wrote in a Facebook post. Paltzik thanked those who sent emails, texts and voice messages in support of Desronvil, while acknowledging that others may disagree with the position he took inside the jury room. CLANCY HOLDOUT JUROR TAPS FORMER TRUMP LAWYER TO FIGHT BACK AS HE’S ‘DRAGGED THROUGH THE MUD’: ATTORNEY "This country was built on intelligent debate in the public square," Paltzik wrote. "That’s the same reason we support the good faith right of an individual juror to follow the evidence and the law to wherever they take him or her, free from fear of reprisal." LINDSAY CLANCY JUDGE INDEFINITELY IMPOUNDS JUROR NAMES, CITING SAFETY AND 'DIVISIVE' ATTENTION The attorney’s latest comments come as the deeply divisive case returns to the national spotlight. Patrick Clancy, the father of the three slain children and Lindsay Clancy’s ex-husband, gave his first television interview on CBS News’ "60 Minutes" Sunday night. Patrick Clancy discussed his grief, memories of his children and baseless conspiracy theories that have spread online since the January 2023 killings. His wife, Dr. Rachel Danis, also appeared in the segment with correspondent Ross Douthat. JUDGE JUDY WARNS OF 'DANGER' IF PROSECUTORS DON'T RETRY LINDSAY CLANCY AFTER MURDER TRIAL ENDS IN MISTRIAL Lindsay Clancy, 36, was tried on three counts of first-degree murder in the deaths of the couple’s children, 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson and 8-month-old Callan. The children were found strangled inside the family’s Duxbury, Massachusetts, home in January 2023. Clancy admitted killing the children, but her attorneys argued she was not criminally responsible because she was suffering from postpartum psychosis. Prosecutors argued that the former labor and delivery nurse understood what she was doing and carried out the killings deliberately. LINDSAY CLANCY JUDGE CALLS MISTRIAL, THEN GRANTS DEFENSE ONE HOUR STAY FOR APPEAL Judge William Sullivan declared a mistrial Sept. 4 after seven days of deliberations. The jury was split 11-1, with 11 jurors prepared to find Clancy not criminally responsible and Desronvil holding out for a conviction. Desronvil later said he had no doubt prosecutors proved their case. LINDSAY CLANCY JUROR ADMITTED 'REASONABLE DOUBT' BUT STILL REFUSED INSANITY VERDICT, FOREPERSON SAYS "Based on all the physical evidence, key witnesses and what the prosecution presents, I thought it was enough proof that she knew exactly what she was doing and planned," Desronvil said in a statement first reported by NewsNation and confirmed to Fox News Digital by Paltzik. Desronvil said he tried to raise different theories during deliberations but was repeatedly cut off by fellow jurors who treated his questions as uncertainty. LINDSAY CLANCY HOLDOUT PRAISED AS 'AMERICAN HERO' BY LAWYER WHO SAYS HE REPRESENTS HIM The fallout from the mistrial quickly spilled beyond the courthouse, with Desronvil facing intense public scrutiny over his refusal to move off his position. Paltzik, who previously represented President Donald Trump in lawsuits against The New York Times, CBS and ABC News, told Fox News Digital that he is focused on Desronvil’s "health, safety and well-being." He has called the juror an "American Hero" and "Champion of Justice." LINDSAY CLANCY LAWYER SAYS HE PLANS NEW MOTION TO DISMISS AFTER JURORS SPEAK OUT ON MISTRIAL: REPORT Former prosecutor and behavioral health law expert Mark Astor previously told Fox News Digital that Desronvil appeared to have hired counsel to defend his name after being "dragged through the mud." "The whole idea of the jury is sort of this sacred arena where jurors get to decide a verdict in a case," Astor said. "And now we’re taking what is really a sacred arena, and we’re exposing it to the public." Plymouth County prosecutors have not announced whether they will retry Clancy. Her defense team has raised the possibility of resolving the case without another trial and brought in veteran Boston attorney Martin Weinberg to pursue a motion seeking dismissal on double-jeopardy grounds. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Clancy is due back in Plymouth Superior Court for a status hearing Sept. 29, when the path forward could become clearer. Fox News Digital's Adam Sabes contributed to this report.

articles.title: Transpetro: inscrições para concurso terminam nesta segunda | G1
articles.standfirst: Prazo para participar da seleção da Transpetro termina às 23h59. Concurso oferece 281 vagas imediatas e 3.890 para cadastro de reserva, com salários de até R$ 15.034,81.
articles.summary: Prazo para participar da seleção da Transpetro termina às 23h59. Concurso oferece 281 vagas imediatas e 3.890 para cadastro de reserva, com salários de até R$ 15.034,81.
articles.body:
Os interessados em participar do concurso público da Transpetro , empresa de transporte da Petrobras , têm até as 23h59 desta segunda-feira (14) para se inscrever.

A seleção oferece 281 vagas imediatas e 3.890 para cadastro de reserva, totalizando 4.171 oportunidades para cargos de níveis médio, técnico e superior nos quadros de terra e mar.

As oportunidades contemplam profissionais de níveis médio, técnico e superior, com remunerações mínimas garantidas que variam de R$ 5.464 a R$ 15.034,81 , além de benefícios como previdência complementar, benefício educacional e plano de saúde.

As inscrições devem ser realizadas exclusivamente pela internet, no site da Fundação Cesgranrio , banca organizadora do certame.

Ao todo, foram publicados quatro editais . Para o quadro de terra, há um processo seletivo para cargos de nível médio/técnico e outro para nível superior. Já para o quadro de mar, um edital é destinado a oficiais e outro a suboficiais e guarnição.

As vagas abrangem áreas como administração, contabilidade, manutenção, enfermagem, engenharia, tecnologia e advocacia, além de cargos marítimos, como auxiliar de saúde, cozinheiro, eletricista, moço de convés, moço de máquinas, taifeiro e oficiais de máquinas e de náutica.

No quadro de terra, a remuneração mínima garantida é de R$ 6.539,54 para nível médio/técnico e de R$ 14.973,62 para nível superior .

No quadro de mar, a remuneração mínima garantida varia conforme o cargo, de R$ 5.464 a R$ 15.034,81 . O maior valor é oferecido para segundo oficial de náutica. Veja abaixo os editais:

A taxa de inscrição varia de acordo com o cargo:

R$ 81,50 — nível médio/técnico: auxiliar de saúde, condutor bombeador, condutor mecânico, cozinheiro, eletricista, moço de convés, moço de máquinas, taifeiro e Profissional Transpetro de Nível Médio – Júnior;

R$ 117 — nível superior: segundo oficial de máquinas, segundo oficial de náutica e Profissional Transpetro de Nível Superior – Júnior.

Candidatos inscritos no CadÚnico e doadores de medula óssea cadastrados em entidades reconhecidas pelo Ministério da Saúde puderam solicitar a isenção da taxa, conforme os prazos estabelecidos nos editais.

Terminal da Transpetro em Brasília, no DF. — Foto: TV Globo

As etapas de seleção variam de acordo com o quadro — Mar ou Terra — e o nível de escolaridade dos cargos.

Os candidatos às oportunidades do quadro de mar passarão por provas objetivas, exame de aptidão física e, quando aplicável, procedimentos de confirmação das condições declaradas para concorrer às vagas reservadas.

As provas objetivas terão questões de conhecimentos específicos e gerais . O conteúdo varia conforme o cargo e pode incluir disciplinas como Língua Portuguesa, Língua Inglesa e Inglês Técnico Marítimo.

Já o exame de aptidão física, exclusivo para o Quadro de Mar, será composto por dois testes:

Corrida de 12 minutos: distância mínima de 1.800 metros para homens e 1.500 metros para mulheres;

Natação: percurso de 25 metros, em estilo livre e sem limite de tempo.

Para os cargos do quadro de terra, não haverá exame de aptidão física . A seleção será feita por meio de provas objetivas e, para os candidatos que concorrerem às vagas reservadas, por uma etapa de confirmação das condições declaradas.

No nível médio, as provas terão 60 questões no total, divididas entre 40 questões de conhecimentos específicos, 10 de Língua Portuguesa e 10 de Matemática. Já no nível superior, serão 70 questões: 50 de conhecimentos específicos, 10 de Língua Portuguesa e 10 de Língua Inglesa.

A exceção é a ênfase de Advocacia : além das 70 questões objetivas, os candidatos também farão uma prova discursiva, composta por duas questões, de caráter eliminatório e classificatório.

Para quem concorrer às vagas reservadas, a seleção prevê avaliação de pessoas com deficiência (PcD), confirmação complementar da autodeclaração de candidatos negros e verificação documental de indígenas e quilombolas.

As provas objetivas estão previstas para 29 de novembro e serão aplicadas em todas as capitais brasileiras e no Distrito Federal.

Os candidatos poderão escolher o local de realização das provas entre as opções disponibilizadas pela banca, independentemente do polo de trabalho para o qual estiverem concorrendo. A duração das provas varia conforme o cargo e o nível de escolaridade:

Nível médio — Quadro de Terra : 4 horas;

Nível superior — Quadro de Terra : 4 horas e 30 minutos;

Advocacia — Quadro de Terra : 5 horas e 30 minutos;

Oficiais — Quadro de Mar : 4 horas e 30 minutos.

Após a aprovação, os candidatos convocados ainda precisarão comprovar os requisitos exigidos para o cargo e passar por exames médicos admissionais . Para os profissionais do quadro de mar, também está previsto teste toxicológico para detecção de substâncias psicoativas.

No quadro de terra, as oportunidades serão distribuídas entre os polos Norte/Nordeste, Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo e Sul. Para o quadro de mar, as vagas terão abrangência nacional.

A distribuição das 281 oportunidades por cargo e polo, assim como os requisitos, etapas de seleção, conteúdo das provas e cronograma, estão detalhados nos editais.

Segundo a Transpetro, os processos seletivos terão validade de um ano e meio, com possibilidade de prorrogação pelo mesmo período .

Os processos seletivos também terão um mecanismo de paridade de gênero na segunda fase . Segundo a companhia, a iniciativa busca reduzir a sub-representação feminina nas carreiras contempladas pelos editais.

Atualmente, cerca de 15% dos empregados da Transpetro são mulheres , enquanto os homens representam aproximadamente 85% do quadro.

A medida será aplicada apenas na composição da segunda etapa. Para chegar a essa fase, todos os candidatos precisarão atingir a nota mínima exigida na primeira etapa. A classificação final continuará considerando o desempenho dos participantes.

Antes da publicação dos quatro editais, foi realizado um sorteio para definir os cargos, áreas e polos aos quais serão destinadas determinadas vagas reservadas a grupos étnico-raciais e pessoas com deficiência (PcD).

De acordo com a Transpetro, 30% das vagas e do cadastro de reserva serão destinados a grupos étnico-raciais, distribuídos da seguinte forma:

Outros 10% são reservados a pessoas com deficiência. Os editais estabelecem, inclusive, a aplicação da reserva de 10% também na formação do cadastro de reserva .

O sorteio foi realizado nos casos em que a quantidade de vagas por cargo, ênfase ou polo não permitia alcançar automaticamente os percentuais de reserva previstos na legislação.

O procedimento não selecionou candidatos nem interfere na classificação nas provas. Ele serviu para definir a alocação das vagas reservadas entre os cargos, ênfases e polos.

articles.title: Greve da Caixa pode acabar; funcionários votam nova proposta | G1
articles.standfirst: Assembleias eletrônicas ocorrem em todo o país e devem terminar às 18h. Saúde Caixa, principal impasse da negociação, teve mudanças em mensalidades e cobranças por atendimento.
articles.summary: Assembleias eletrônicas ocorrem em todo o país e devem terminar às 18h. Saúde Caixa, principal impasse da negociação, teve mudanças em mensalidades e cobranças por atendimento.
articles.body:
Agência da Caixa de Mogi das Cruzes tem avisos de greve — Foto: Beatriz Andreoli/TV Diário

Os funcionários da Caixa Econômica Federal participam nesta segunda-feira (21) de assembleias eletrônicas em todo o país para decidir se aceitam a nova proposta apresentada pelo banco para renovação do Acordo Coletivo de Trabalho (ACT).

A votação, prevista para terminar às 18h, poderá definir o fim ou a continuidade da greve, iniciada em 10 de setembro.

O principal ponto em discussão é o Saúde Caixa, plano de saúde dos empregados, que se tornou o maior impasse nas negociações entre o banco e os representantes dos trabalhadores.

Pela proposta apresentada, a contribuição dos titulares passará a ser de 3,7% da remuneração-base a partir de 2027. Para os dependentes diretos, a mensalidade será de R$ 560.

R$ 660 para filhos entre 21 e 24 anos considerados dependentes indiretos;

R$ 900 para filhos de 24 a 27 anos e pais ou mães remanescentes.

O limite de contribuição do grupo familiar, formado pelo titular e dependentes diretos, ficará em 9%.

Em relação à proposta anterior, a Caixa também reduziu de R$ 150 para R$ 120 a cobrança por consulta em pronto atendimento e manteve a isenção de coparticipação na telemedicina.

Outro ponto aceito pelo banco foi a previsão de pelo menos um empregado dedicado exclusivamente ao Saúde Caixa em cada Gerência de Pessoas (Gipes) e em cada Representação Regional de Pessoas (Repes).

Além das mudanças no plano de saúde, a Caixa apresentou ajustes no programa de remuneração variável Super Caixa.

Entre as medidas previstas para o segundo semestre deste ano estão a ampliação da premiação inicial por habilitação, que passará de 25% para 50%, mudanças nos critérios de avaliação e maior transparência nos painéis de resultados.

O banco também informou que não haverá penalização relacionada aos programas Figital e Genesys em 2026. Segundo a proposta, os projetos continuarão em fase piloto e seguirão sendo discutidos com representantes dos empregados antes da definição das regras para 2027.

A Caixa manteve ainda a oferta de um prêmio extraordinário de R$ 3 mil por empregado, vinculado à superação de metas operacionais já atingidas neste ano.

Segundo os sindicatos, a proposta preserva todas as cláusulas já previstas nos acordos coletivos e na Convenção Coletiva de Trabalho (CCT) da categoria.

Greve começou após rejeição de proposta anterior

Os funcionários da Caixa estão em greve nacional desde 10 de setembro , após rejeitarem a proposta anterior de renovação do Acordo Coletivo de Trabalho.

A paralisação começou após mais de 90% das bases sindicais rejeitarem a oferta apresentada pelo banco , de acordo com a Contraf-CUT. O Saúde Caixa era apontado pelas entidades como um dos principais pontos de discordância nas negociações.

Enquanto os empregados da Caixa decidiram entrar em greve por tempo indeterminado, a categoria bancária como um todo já havia assinado a Convenção Coletiva de Trabalho com a Federação Nacional dos Bancos (Fenaban).

O acordo prevê reposição da inflação pelo INPC e aumento real de 0,6% por dois anos, além de medidas relacionadas à saúde mental, ao combate ao assédio e ao direito à desconexão.

Caso a proposta seja aprovada pelos trabalhadores nas assembleias desta segunda-feira, a expectativa das entidades sindicais é que a greve seja encerrada e as medidas negociadas sejam implementadas.

articles.title: Iluminação valoriza revestimentos e transforma os ambientes | G1
articles.standfirst: Luz natural e iluminação artificial influenciam a percepção de cores, texturas e acabamentos antes e depois da obra.
articles.summary: Luz natural e iluminação artificial influenciam a percepção de cores, texturas e acabamentos antes e depois da obra.
articles.body:
Escolher um revestimento vai muito além da cor ou do formato da peça. A iluminação do ambiente, por exemplo, exerce um papel decisivo na forma como porcelanatos, pedras e revestimentos serão percebidos ao longo do dia. Um mesmo material pode apresentar tonalidades, contrastes e texturas diferentes conforme a incidência da luz natural ou o tipo de iluminação artificial utilizada no projeto.

Essa influência tem sido considerada cada vez mais cedo por arquitetos e designers de interiores. Em salas, banheiros, cozinhas e áreas integradas, a combinação entre revestimento e iluminação ajuda a valorizar relevos, elementos decorativos, destacar veios inspirados em pedras naturais e ampliar a percepção de continuidade proporcionada pelos grandes formatos.

A incidência da luz pode alterar a percepção das cores, dos relevos e das texturas de um mesmo revestimento — Foto: Acervo Vilarejo

Enquanto a iluminação quente tende a realçar tons amadeirados e criar uma sensação mais acolhedora, a iluminação fria evidencia detalhes, contrastes e texturas com maior nitidez. Esse comportamento interfere diretamente na leitura dos materiais e explica por que um revestimento pode apresentar uma aparência diferente daquela observada em catálogos ou fotografias.

Pensando nisso, a Vilarejo disponibiliza em suas lojas mesas de especificação que permitem visualizar os revestimentos sob diferentes temperaturas de luz. Durante a escolha dos materiais, clientes e profissionais podem comparar o comportamento das peças em iluminação quente e fria, aproximando a decisão das condições que serão encontradas após a instalação no ambiente.

As mesas de especificação da Vilarejo ajudam a comparar os materiais em diferentes condições de iluminação antes da definição do projeto — Foto: Acervo Vilarejo

Esse cuidado evita surpresas após a obra e contribui para escolhas mais alinhadas ao resultado esperado. Em revestimentos inspirados em pedras naturais, madeiras e concretos, por exemplo, a luz pode destacar nuances e relevos que fazem toda a diferença na composição do ambiente.

A arquitetura é construída pela combinação de diferentes elementos, e a iluminação é um deles. Quando materiais e luz são pensados em conjunto, os espaços revelam texturas, profundidade e detalhes que muitas vezes passam despercebidos durante a escolha inicial.

articles.summary: O Brasil precisa reduzir ainda mais o desmatamento de nossas florestas e decidir qual modelo queremos para a extração de petróleo na margem equatorial.
articles.body:
Estamos às vésperas de enfrentar um super El Niño, um fenômeno que pode ser o mais forte em mais de 100 anos. O El Niño é um evento que ocorre de tempos em tempos, mas este tem um agravante: o aquecimento global. A revista Science, uma das mais respeitadas do mundo, publicou um estudo que confirma que a crise climática provocada pela queima de combustíveis fósseis agrava os efeitos desse fenômeno. E o Brasil tem muito a ver com isso. É urgente que o país tenha maior capacidade de lidar com os eventos climáticos extremos – eventos que causam tantos danos, como vimos recentemente na Amazônia e no Rio Grande do Sul. Mas também precisamos reduzir ainda mais o desmatamento de nossas florestas e temos que decidir qual modelo queremos para a extração de petróleo na margem equatorial. Ou seja, a pauta ambiental que vencer esta eleição pode influenciar o futuro de todo o planeta.

Neste episódio, Natuza Nery conversa com André Trigueiro, jornalista da TV Globo e editor do programa Cidade e Soluções da GloboNews. Especialista na cobertura ambiental, Trigueiro comenta as propostas (e a falta delas) dos candidatos nesta pauta. Também neste episódio você ouvirá trechos das entrevistas que o produtor Marco Antonio Martins conduziu com os especialistas Suely Araújo, Ricardo Abramovay, Mercedes Bustamante e Natalie Unterstell.

Her candid response also touched on fertility expectations and personal boundaries. She also opened up about her mental health, revealing that she is currently seeing two therapists.Pokimane calls out viewers over questions about having childrenPokimane expressed frustration with viewers who repeatedly ask about her plans for motherhood. She pointed out that questions about boyfriends, marriage, and children can cross a line, especially when people assume women must follow a certain timeline.During her stream, she challenged the double standard and questioned whether people hold men to the same expectations.Pokimane said:"I think sometimes people… Actually, let me rephrase this. I think sometimes people don’t realize how silly their questions are and, like, a little invasive. Like, 'Are you actually my mom? Where’s your boyfriend? Where are your kids? Are you okay?' It’s more dependent on how much you take care of yourself."Pokimane then questioned why viewers were so invested in other people's family plans, suggesting they could ask more meaningful questions instead.She added:"I don’t know. articles.title: Far-right tops another German state vote, Merz party routed
articles.summary: Europe News: SCHWERIN (GERMANY): The Alternative for Germany (AfD) took first place in state elections in northeastern Germany Sunday, exit polls showed, deliverin.
articles.body: SCHWERIN (GERMANY): The Alternative for Germany (AfD) took first place in state elections in northeastern Germany Sunday, exit polls showed, delivering a "disaster" for Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who vowed to push ahead with his reform agenda.The AfD was set to win 37% in the state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, ahead of the centre-left Social Democrats on 35.5% and far in front of Merz's conservatives, who got 5.5% and barely crossed the threshold to enter the state parliament, according to exit polls on ARD public television. But the far-right party is unlikely to govern as the other main parties rule out working with it.If confirmed, Sunday's result would be the worst in any state election for Merz's party since 1949. It would also be another first-place finish at state level in a month for the AfD party, which is shunned by mainstream parties but is topping national opinion polls. "It's a disaster," Merz said in televised remarks, but signalled that he would fight on as chancellor after speculation that a bad result could prompt him to resign.In another election in the capital Berlin that also took place Sunday, the far-left Linke party was on 24.5%, while Merz's conservatives were on 20% and the AfD also gained in strength, hitting 16%.Sunday's results may not prove a knock-out blow for Merz. But his low approval ratings, unpopular reforms and the triumph of the AfD in an earlier state election in Saxony-Anhalt have left his future in the balance.Merz has called a party meeting for Sunday to discuss the way forward.The elections in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, a largely rural state in the formerly communist east, and the capital Berlin follow the Sept 6 election in Saxony-Anhalt, where the AfD came close to the rare feat of winning an absolute majority. Elections in the two states would not usually draw much interest outside Germany, but the AfD's success in Saxony-Anhalt, which it sees as the first step towards winning federal elections due in 2029, has sent shock waves through Europe. In just over a decade, the party, which wants to take tough action to deport foreigners with no right to stay in Germany, restore energy ties with Russia and quit the euro, has transformed itself from a fringe eurosceptic movement to the country's most popular party. reutersCatch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: ICE agent shoots and wounds man in Texas as locals demand answers
articles.summary: Protests broke out after a Venezuelan man was taken to hospital with a gunshot wound in his torso.
articles.body:
Protesters have gathered in Austin, Texas where local officials said a US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent shot and wounded a man in the Texas capital.

Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, a 28-year-old Venezuelan national, was shot in the torso and taken to hospital, his lawyer has told US media.

Local officials are seeking answers from federal authorities, and could not say whether he was a target of ICE. The mayor and police have demanded an independent probe, with this shooting coming months after a man in Houston, Texas was shot dead by an ICE officer.

The BBC has contacted ICE and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

What is ICE and what powers do its agents have to use force?

Attorney Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch told CBS that Garces Perez called his wife while "yelling in pain" in hospital. She told National Public Radio he was in ICE custody.

The shooting on Sunday in Austin occurred just before 1300 local time, although details remain scarce. Dozens of protesters, some waving the flags of Mexico and Guatemala, have since gathered at the scene carrying signs demanding that ICE leave Austin.

Local television outlets showed the demonstrators gathering across the street from ​a blue Toyota Corolla that ⁠sustained damage to the passenger-side door, as ICE agents stood nearby, Reuters news agency reported.

Mayor Kirk Watson, a Democrat, said that Austinites have a right to know what happened and "a right to feel safe in their city" during a media briefing on Sunday.

"They should know the truth" he said, adding that he is pleased that the city will also be involved in the investigation.

He added that ICE operations have surged in Austin in recent weeks. ICE has faced intense scrutiny after a number of deadly shootings, including the death of Houston resident Lorenzo Salgado Araujo. Salgado Araujo had not been a target of an ICE investigation, but was shot during an ICE traffic stop, according to DHS .

Texas Congressman Greg Casar, a Democrat, has demanded a full and immediate independent investigation and the release of body camera footage. He also demanded "accountability for any ICE officer who broke the law".

The Austin Police Department confirmed to a local CBS News affiliate that the victim was injured and was transported to hospital. No Austin police officer was involved in the shooting.

The Trump administration has ramped up immigration enforcement efforts and arrests during Trump's second term, which sparked unrest across several US cities.

The administration has defended its policies and the agency's controversial tactics as necessary for public safety and to carry out Trump's mass deportations mandate.

But rights activists say that the administration has violated free speech and due process rights and Democrats have demanded reforms at the agency, including requiring immigration enforcement agents to wear body cameras and barring them from concealing their faces during operations.

Earlier this month the US Department of Justice charged an ICE agent with lying about the non-fatal shooting of a Venezuelan migrant in Minnesota - a rare instance in which the current justice department accused a federal agent of breaking the law on the job.

Earlier this week, Florida lawmaker Maria Elvira Salazar, a Republican who has been spoken out against the immigration crackdown, released an advert critcising the targeting and detaining of individuals who have no criminal record.

Salazar appeared on the CBS programme Face the Nation on Sunday and said that she has since spoken to the president, and believes he will keep the country on the right track.

"He gets it more than anybody," she said.

articles.title: Beaumont Lamarre-Condon: Trial of ex-cop accused of double murder to begin in Sydney
articles.summary: Beaumont Lamarre-Condon has pleaded not guilty to the 2024 murder of his ex-partner and his new boyfriend.
articles.body:
The double murder trial of Beaumont Lamarre-Condon, a former police officer accused of killing his ex-partner and his new boyfriend in 2024, is to begin in Sydney on Monday.

Lamarre-Condon, 31, has pleaded not guilty to two charges of domestic violence-related murder and one of aggravated break and enter.

Police allege Lamarre-Condon used his work-issued gun to shoot his ex-partner Jesse Baird, 26, a television presenter, and Baird's new partner Luke Davies, 29, a Qantas flight attendant, at a home in the inner Sydney suburb of Paddington.

The couple's bodies were found in a rural area more than 200km southwest of Sydney, hidden in surfboard bags. The trial is expected to run for three months.

Police launched a frantic search for Baird and Davies after bloodied items belonging to the couple were found in a bin in Sydney's south in February 2024.

Later that week, Lamarre-Condon handed himself in to a police station and was charged with the alleged murders.

Eight days after the alleged killings took place, authorities found the couple's bodies.

Lamarre-Condon was sacked by New South Wales (NSW) Police in the weeks after he was charged with the alleged murders.

A jury is expected to be selected on Monday, followed by opening statements by the prosecutors and the defence.

articles.title: ICE officer shoots, wounds man in Austin; protesters demand probe
articles.summary: US News: A US Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer shot and wounded a man in Austin, Texas, on Sunday during a brief foot pursuit, local officials said,.
articles.body: A US Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer shot and wounded a man in Austin, Texas, on Sunday during a brief foot pursuit, local officials said, as the incident drew protests and calls for an independent investigation.The man, identified by immigration attorney Kate Lincoln Goldfinch as 28-year-old Venezuelan Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, was shot once in the torso and remained in serious but stable condition at a hospital, officials said.Austin Police Chief Lisa Davis said the shooting happened after a traffic stop in northern Austin. She cautioned that information about the incident was still preliminary. Austin police were not involved in the shooting, although local investigators were at the scene.Mayor Kirk Watson said he was “very angry and extremely disappointed” that a person had been shot by ICE in Austin, adding that the city had seen a “significant increase, almost overnight” in ICE operations.Watson said he wanted Austin police and other local authorities involved in the investigation rather than leaving it solely to ICE.“I will say, frankly, from my perspective, the credibility of ICE doing some form of investigation just by itself and excluding others would not be appropriate,” Watson said.US Rep Greg Casar, a Democrat representing parts of Austin, had called for an independent investigation shortly after the shooting was reported. He later sent a letter to the Department of Homeland Security seeking an immediate, independent probe, the release of all footage from the shooting and accountability for any wrongdoing by the agent involved.“The horror has come to our city: ICE has shot a person in Austin this morning,” Casar wrote on X, adding that he wanted “truth, transparency and accountability.”The Travis County district attorney's office also asked for local police and prosecutors to participate in the investigation and requested access to evidence held by federal authorities.The Department of Homeland Security, which oversees ICE, did not immediately provide details about the shooting.Goldfinch said she believed Garces Perez had no criminal history or final order of removal, although she later said she did not know his current immigration status.The attorney said Garces Perez's family initially struggled to obtain information from the hospital. His wife was later informed that he had been released into ICE custody several hours after the shooting. It was not immediately clear whether he remained at the hospital or had been transferred elsewhere.About 100 protesters gathered near the shooting site as a large law enforcement presence remained in the area. A dark blue Toyota Corolla with damage to its passenger-side door and what appeared to be bullet holes was later towed away.The Austin incident follows other shootings involving immigration agents. In July, an ICE officer fatally shot 52-year-old Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Houston after federal agents pursued him in unmarked vehicles.Another ICE officer shot 25-year-old Colombian man Johan Sebastián in Maine in July. The administration's immigration crackdown has also faced widespread criticism following the deaths of Alex Pretti and Renee Good in Minnesota.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
